Macworld

Apple has had a busy fall, with the launch of the iPhone Duo, HomeView smart hub, and the M5 Ultra Mac Studio. But there’s one more event this week, and it might be the biggest of all. And you can follow every rumor and announcement with us right here.

Apple kicked off its week of releases on Monday with the new iPad mini, which got a thinner design, new A20 Pro chip, and an OLED display. As you can guess by the thinly veiled pun, this week’s marquee announcement is a new MacBook Pro, but not just any MacBook Pro. Here’s what else we’re expecting to see:

Touchscreen MacBook Pro: After years of denials, Apple appears to be on the verge of releasing its first-ever touchscreen MacBook. Rumors say it will have a new design with a lighter chassis, Dynamic Island, and an OLED display. And a very high price tag.

M6 iMac: Apple announced the M6 chip in the Mac mini last month and now it’ll reportedly make its way into the iMac. There could be new colors too.

M6 MacBook Pro: The entry-level MacBook Pro gets its annual chip-and-ship upgrade.

Pro and Tell event: Live blog

35 mins ago, By Michael Simon

Later launch on Wednesday

If you look at the pre-order times for the new iPad mini, iMac and MacBook Pro, you’ll see that they start at 10:10 am PT tomorrow. That also lines up with Apple’s hands-on event happening in LA at 10 am PT. So you probably don’t need to wake up early tomorrow to get a look at the touchscreen MacBook Pro. I’m pretty sure it won’t pop up on Apple’s website until 10 am PT/1 pm PT.

1 hour ago, By Michael Simon

Apple's 'exciting' week isn't very exciting (yet)

After the iPhone Duo and Homeview, this final product launch of 2026 isn’t all that exciting, despite Greg Joswiak’s promise. At least not yet. Now that Apple has gotten the iPad mini, iMac, and MacBook Pro out of the way, the stage is set for the first-ever touchscreen MacBook Pro, which should bring a slew of exciting changes to Apple’s high-end laptop. Along with the touchscreen, there is expected to be a new design that’s much lighter, an upgraded hinge that doesn’t wobble when touched, and an OLED display. Now that’s exciting.

2 hours ago, By Michael Simon

Upgrade for Final Cut Pro users

In addition to the new iMac and MacBook Pro, Apple updated Creator Studio today with several new features, most notably building MotionVFX into Final Cut Pro. Apple purchased MotionVFX earlier this year, but the plugin remained a $29/month plugin. Now that’s free, “giving editors access to thousands of elements, including templates with unique themes, stylish graphics, titles, and transitions, as well as tools for rotoscoping, tracking, and color grading,” for the same price as before.

2 hours ago, By Michael Simon

Where are the new colors?

We’ve been reading reports about new iMac colors for years now, but they have yet to arrive. The new M6 models have the same seven “vibrant” colors: blue, purple, pink, orange, yellow, green, and silver. There’s nothing wrong with those options, but why would Apple test new colors but not release them? Anyway, here are your iMac options probably for the next 2-3 years:

Faster Ethernet in the iMac

One small change in the iMac: The base model is now configurable up to 2.5 Gigabit Ethernet rather than 1 Gigabit Ethernet in the previous models. The four-port model comes with 2.5 Gigabit standard.

3 hours ago, By Michael Simon

Same MacBook Pro, new chip

Like the iMacs, the M6 MacBook Pro is identical to the M5 model, with a new chip and Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6. Otherwise you’re getting the exact same machine. But in these times, I’m thankful the price hasn’t increased.

3 hours ago, By Michael Simon

Just a new chip

The new iMac is very much the old iMac with a new chip. The colors, storage capacity, memory, display, and features are all the same. The only thing that’s improved is the wireless connectivity due to the N1 chip. Now you’ll get Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6.

3 hours ago, By Michael Simon

Apple launches new M6 iMac and MacBook Pro

As expected, Apple has announced M6 upgrades to the MacBook Pro and iMac, with the same starting prices ($1,499 for the iMac and $1,999 for the MacBook Pro). I’m off to dive into the specs, but at first glance it seems to be a very minor update.

3 hours ago, By Michael Simon

How much will the new Macs cost?

Apple is expected to announce updates to the iMac and MacBook Pro this morning with new chips, possibly new colors, and probably a few other new features. But the question I have is, how much will they cost? Apple’s entry-level MacBook Pro already got a $300 bump in June, but Apple raised the price of the Mac mini, Apple TV 4K, and HomePod after their own bumps, so it’s possible the new M6 MacBook Pro crosses the $2,000.

The iMac currently starts at $1,499 with two Thunderbolt ports and a downgraded M4 with 8 cores, while the higher-end 10-core model with 4 Thunderbolt ports starts at $1,699. Both have 256GB hard drives. I wouldn’t be surprised to see the entry-level model axes and the storage increased to 1TB for a new starting price of $1,999.

4 hours ago, By David Price

The drawback of thinness

One of the many significant upgrades to the iPad mini announced yesterday was a redesign that sees the device drop from 6.3mm to 5.4mm thick. (It’s also shed 13 percent of its weight.) As my colleague Michael Simon pointed out yesterday, that puts the mini in the same ultra-slim company as the iPhone Air, unfolded iPhone Duo, and iPad Pro.

But of course there are drawbacks to this slimming down–and I’m not talking about lower battery life (which we’ll certainly test) or a tendency to bend (which other people who don’t mind damaging their loan units will certainly test). I’m talking about case compatibility.

Apple has added a new product to its online store called Smart Folio for iPad mini (A20 Pro). This accessory is certified as compatible with that model and no other. Will your existing cases work on the new iPad mini? Maybe (considering that the length and width are almost identical, and that many iPad cases attach on the back rather than completely enclosing the device), and maybe not. Best to give Apple $79 just to be on the safe side. Don’t complain. It’s thinner.

5 hours ago, By David Price

M6: What's the big deal?

Assuming today goes the way we expect, the next set of announcements will focus heavily on the upgrades delivered by the M6 processor. This is part of Apple’s latest chip generation, and made its first appearance, to critical acclaim, in the Mac mini in August. So what’s the big deal?

The key factor here is that the M6 is the first of Apple’s chips to use the new 2nm manufacturing process from TSMC, which allows the company to increase core counts and add features while making the chip smaller than the M5. It also lets the chip run at lower power and higher clock speeds. Today’s new iMac and MacBook Pro could be looking at both greater processing muscle and improved power efficiency, and that’s a killer combination by anyone’s standards.

If you want all the details about this exciting new chip and the benefits it brings, Macworld’s Jason Cross spent some time doing a thorough M6 deep dive.

M6 MacBook Pro processor: What does M6 change?

The M6 uses a 2nm manufacturing process, increasing transistor density, and features a 12-core CPU comprising two super cores, four performance cores, and six efficiency cores. That’s up from the M5’s 10-core CPU. Apple’s Mac mini M6 announcement claimed up to 20 percent faster multithreaded performance than M5, although that testing used a Mac mini. Read more about the M6 in our M6 deep dive.

Graphics also get a boost, with a 12-core GPU replacing the M5’s 10-core version. Neural Accelerators and hardware-accelerated ray tracing return, while memory bandwidth increases from 153GB/s to up to 170GB/s, allowing data to move more quickly between the chip and unified memory.

The M6 introduces a dual 16-core Neural Engine, compared with the M5’s single 16-core engine. For this laptop, Apple reports up to 1.9 times faster Neural Engine performance and 25 percent faster on-device AI workloads versus M5. These are separate measures of performance, with the benefits depending on the task and how an app uses the chip.

The Media Engine retains the M5’s listed capabilities, including hardware acceleration for H.264, HEVC, ProRes, and ProRes RAW, alongside AV1 decoding. Dedicated video encoding and decoding hardware helps handle demanding media tasks efficiently, but Apple’s comparison sheet lists no new codec support for M6.

M6 MacBook Pro RAM: How much memory does it have?

The M6 MacBook Pro starts with 16GB of unified memory, with 24GB and 32GB configurations also available – the same capacities offered with M5. However, memory bandwidth increases from 153GB/s to up to 170GB/s, helping the chip access data more quickly.

Additional unified memory gives applications and graphics workloads more room to operate simultaneously. For local AI, capacity affects which models fit in memory, while bandwidth affects how quickly data can move.

Buying advice: Choose 16GB for everyday productivity; consider 24GB for heavier multitasking and creative work, or 32GB for memory-intensive projects and local AI experimentation.

M6 MacBook Pro Connectivity: What ports and wireless options are there?

Wireless connectivity improves with Wi-Fi 7 (802.11be) and Bluetooth 6, replacing the M5 model’s Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 5.3. Wi-Fi 7 availability varies by country.

The physical connections remain unchanged, including three Thunderbolt 4 (USB-C) ports, HDMI, an SDXC card slot, and a 3.5mm headphone jack with support for high-impedance headphones.

Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported that Apple will announce the M6 iMac on October 27, 2026.

On October 19, Apple announced a media event, dubbed “Pro and Tell” on October 28, 2026. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman previously indicated that another Apple product launch was planned for Tuesday, October 27, so an announcement could still take place the day before the media gathering.

The M6 iMac is among the products expected to make an appearance, alongside new MacBook Pro M6 models, a touchscreen MacBook Pro, and an updated iPad mini.

The prospect of an imminent iMac launch follows earlier reporting from Gurman. In the Q&A section of his August 23 Power On newsletter, Gurman indicated that the M6 iMac was close to launch and that customers should be able to buy one before the end of 2026.

An earlier July 2026 report also identified two iMac models, codenamed J833 and J834, among a wave of new Macs Apple was preparing.

The current M4 iMac arrived in fall 2024, making it nearly two years old. Apple appears to have skipped an M5 iMac altogether, as it previously skipped the M2 generation, meaning the next model should move directly from M4 to M6.

M6 iMac design: Will there be new colors?

  • Expected: The same 24-inch design, potentially with new color options.

Apple

Anyone hoping for a completely redesigned iMac may be disappointed. According to Gurman’s August reporting, Apple is not preparing a major overhaul of its all-in-one desktop for 2026.

The iMac has retained essentially the same ultra-thin, colorful design since Apple introduced the 24-inch M1 iMac in 2021. Although the M4 iMac update in 2024 introduced some refinements, the overall appearance remained largely unchanged.

Gurman expects the M6 iMac to follow a similar pattern, with the new chip representing the most significant upgrade. However, he has suggested that new colors could be introduced.

Apple currently offers the iMac in seven colors: blue, green, pink, silver, yellow, orange and purple. These options have been available since 2021, although Apple refreshed the shades with the M4 model.

A more substantial iMac redesign could still arrive in a future generation, but there is currently little evidence to suggest that Apple is planning one for the M6 iMac.

M6 iMac display: Will it have a larger screen?

Foundry

  • Expected: A 24-inch 4.5K Retina display, similar to the current model.

The current model features a 24-inch 4.5K Retina display, with a resolution of 4,480 by 2,520 pixels. It uses LED-backlit LCD technology and supports up to 500 nits of brightness. The M6 iMac is likely to retain a similar screen.

There have been rumors about Apple developing a larger iMac with more advanced display technology. In 2023, analyst Ming-Chi Kuo predicted a higher-end 32-inch iMac with a mini-LED display, potentially arriving in 2025. However, that product never materialized, and there is no reliable indication that it will launch alongside the M6 iMac.

M6 iMac specs and performance: How much faster will it be?

  • Expected: M6 chip, improved CPU and GPU performance, faster memory and a substantial AI upgrade.

The M6 iMac may not look very different from its predecessor, but the processor could make it a considerably more powerful computer.

Apple introduced the M6 chip in August 2026, with the new M6 Mac mini going on sale in September. That means we already have a useful indication of the technology the next iMac could include. You can read about how the Mac mini M6 chips compare to other Macs in our Best Mac guide.

The M6 is Apple’s first chip manufactured using a 2-nanometer process, replacing the 3-nanometer technology used by the M4. The smaller manufacturing process allows Apple to improve transistor density, performance and power efficiency.

The M6 used in the Mac mini features:

  • A 12-core CPU.
  • A 12-core GPU with Neural Accelerators in every core.
  • A Dual 16-core Neural Engine for AI and machine-learning tasks.
  • 16GB of standard unified memory, configurable up to 32GB.
  • Memory bandwidth of up to 170GB/s.
  • Improved storage performance compared with the M4 generation.

The M4 iMac currently offers an 8-core or 10-core CPU and an 8-core or 10-core GPU, depending on the configuration. Moving to the M6 could therefore bring a particularly noticeable performance improvement, especially for buyers upgrading from the entry-level M4 model.

Apple claims that the M6 Mac mini delivers up to 40 percent faster CPU performance, twice the graphics performance and four times the AI performance of the M4 Mac mini in its specified tests.

We can’t assume that the M6 iMac will achieve identical results, but these figures demonstrate the potential benefits of moving from the M4 to the M6 generation.

Improved AI performance

One of the biggest improvements could be the M6’s new AI-processing architecture.

Previous M-series chips used a single 16-core Neural Engine. The M6 introduces a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, supported by Neural Accelerators in each GPU core.

Together, these changes should make the M6 iMac significantly better equipped for demanding AI workloads, including running local language models, processing images and using AI-powered creative tools.

For everyday users, the benefits may be less immediately obvious. However, the additional processing capabilities could become increasingly useful as macOS and third-party applications adopt more sophisticated on-device AI features.

More memory and faster connectivity

The M6 supports up to 32GB of unified memory and memory bandwidth of 170GB/s. Whether Apple offers the same memory configurations in the iMac remains to be seen.

The new Mac mini also includes Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, so these connectivity improvements seem likely to arrive on the M6 iMac as well.

It’s unknown if Apple will update the iMac’s Thunderbolt ports, storage options or other hardware features.

M6 iMac price: How much will it cost?

  • Expected starting price: Around $1,499.

When Apple introduced the M4 iMac in 2024, prices started at $1,299 for the entry-level model with an 8-core CPU, 8-core GPU and 256GB of storage. The higher-end version, featuring a 10-core CPU and 10-core GPU, started at $1,499.

However, Apple increased the prices of the M4 iMac in June 2026. The entry-level model now starts at $1,499, while the four-port version starts at $1,699.

These price increases make it difficult to predict what Apple will charge for the next generation.

Apple could retain the current starting prices, particularly if the M6 update introduces relatively few changes beyond the processor. Alternatively, the higher cost of components and memory could result in further increases.

For now, $1,499 is a reasonable starting point for expectations.

Should you buy an M4 iMac or wait for the M6?

  • Our recommendation: Wait for the M6 iMac if you can.

With the next iMac potentially arriving before the end of October, we’d recommend holding off on buying the M4 model at full price.

The current iMac remains an excellent all-in-one desktop for everyday computing, home working, students and families. Its 24-inch Retina display, compact design and M4 processor make it more than capable of handling most people’s needs.

However, the M6 looks set to bring a meaningful increase in performance. The move from M4 to M6 should provide improvements to CPU and GPU performance, while the upgraded Neural Engine could make a difference as AI features become more demanding.

Waiting will also allow you to compare the new iMac’s pricing and specifications with those of the outgoing model. Even if you ultimately choose an M4 iMac, its replacement could make discounted older models more appealing.

There are reasons to buy now. If you need a new Mac immediately and find a substantial discount on an M4 iMac, it could still be a sensible purchase. But for anyone buying a new iMac at full price, waiting for Apple’s next announcement is the better option.

After weeks of development with enrolled beta testers, iOS 27.2 is available to all iPhone users as a stable release, along with macOS, iPadOS, watchOS, and tvOS. The first major update to iOS 27 introduces several handy enhancements to Siri AI, along with some major additions to Apple TV and HomePod.

What happened to iOS 27.1?

It’s odd for Apple to jump from iOS 27.0.1 to iOS 27.2, but there’s a simple explanation: iOS 27.1 was strictly for the iPhone Duo. There was never a developer or public beta release, but Apple likely had a similar program for the software in-house as to not leak specific features for the folding phone. In fact, iPhone Duo users had to update to a newer build of iOS 27.1 after unboxing their phones. 

iOS 27.2 is compatible with all iPhones, including the Duo, so iOS 27.1 might go down as the shortest-lived update Apple has ever released.

Siri AI expansion

Siri AI first launched with iOS 27.0, unlocking a comprehensive chatbot experience in a dedicated app—plus the ability to recall personal data and take in-app action. The initial version, however, was limited to a single language. While the assistant could comprehend many languages when texting it, its main interface and voice commands only supported English. With iOS 27.2, Siri AI officially expands language support to include French, Spanish, Portuguese, Japanese, and Korean.

The latest update also expands what Siri AI can do in Apple’s native communication apps. In Messages, Siri now suggests relevant actions under individual texts when needed. For example, if someone mentions a date, the assistant will surface a shortcut to quickly add it to the Calendar app. Meanwhile, the Phone app’s Call Context feature now highlights saved anniversaries, a welcome addition to the existing birthday reminders.

Another new feature is Siri’s ability to reference previous queries. Siri will now be able to access prior chats even when not continuing a conversation in the Siri app.

iOS 27.2 should also expand Siri AI’s platform availability, unlocking it on the second-generation Apple TV 4K and newer models. Once you install the latest iOS and tvOS builds, your Apple TV 4K will rely on your nearby iPhone to handle personal requests on the big screen. It’s worth noting, however, that Siri AI has yet to be activated on the tvOS 27.2 Release Candidate at the time of writing, and since the new Apple TV doesn’t release until November 13, it may require a separate update.

Mahmoud Itani/Foundry

Apple TV profiles

Speaking of Apple TV, iOS 27.2 brings a highly requested feature to the streaming service. Similar to Netflix, the TV app on your iPhone now allows you to create multiple viewer profiles tied to a single Apple Account.

If you tend to share your personal iPhone or iPad with a family member, they will be able to use your subscription to watch original movies and series without altering your queue or watch history. This does not impact the existing Family Sharing perk that allows up to six independent Apple Accounts to take advantage of a single subscription on their own devices.

Some of the features supported by Apple TV profiles include picking a name and avatar, restricting adult content, adding a 4-digit PIN, and setting autoplay defaults. Notably, the primary account holder will be able to view, manage, and delete any of the secondary profiles created using their account.

Sound Glow on HomePods

The latest OS update revitalizes all HomePod models except the original full-size model from 2018. Once you install iOS and HomePod Software 27.2, you’ll be able to toggle a new Sound Glow setting in the iPhone’s built-in Home app. 

The feature distills a playing song’s album art into a color blob that animates on the HomePod’s top display in sync with the rhythm. While Sound Glow doesn’t affect the actual audio, it does make vibing to music more fun—especially in pitch-black environments, which amplify the dramatic effect.

Other handy HomePod options in the OS 27.2 release include a Lock Controls toggle that disables the touchscreen. If your smart speaker suffers from ghost touch issues, you’ll be able to make it usable again by turning off touch input. 

Mahmoud Itani/Foundry

App Switcher on watchOS

After updating your iPhone, you’ll want to install watchOS 27.2 on your Apple Watch. This release brings back the App Switcher on watchOS after version 27.0 removed it, making it possible to force-quit misbehaving apps again.

It’s not as simple as before, however. Instead of double-clicking the Digital Crown, you’ll now have to tap and hold on the bottom of the screen inside an app to reveal the App Switcher. The retired mechanism will be reassigned to the Apple Watch Series 12’s Live Rewind feature when it debuts later this year.

Mahmoud Itani/Foundry

Apple Pencil support for iPhone Duo

Even though the iPhone Duo only just hit stores a couple of days ago, there’s already an update and it’s a pretty big one. You can now use your Apple Pencil on either Duo screen and attach it to the side like the iPad. However, only the USB-C Apple Pencil works with the Duo, so you miss out on a few Apple Pencil Pro features, including pressure sensitivity and double-tap/squeeze gestures.

Where’s the new Health app?

If you’ve been following Apple news, you may have read about the revamped Health app that surfaced during the iOS 27.2 beta cycle. While it has been removed from iOS 27.2’s final build, the overhauled app appears to still be on track to arrive later this year, as Apple originally promised. It will most likely reappear in iOS 27.3, due to launch in December.

Even if you don’t heavily use Siri AI, Apple TV, or HomePod, we advise you to install iOS 27.2 to apply the bug fixes and security patches (over 150 in iOS alone) included with this release. To get started, go to the Settings app on an iPhone 11 or later, followed by General, then Software Update. Hit the Update button and keep your iPhone connected to a power source until the installation completes.

Apple unveiled iOS 27 at WWDC on June 8, 2026, with the public release following on September 14. But more features are on the way, and the latest beta offers a preview of what’s coming next.

iOS 27 mainly focuses on three key areas: Siri AI, a rebuilt assistant with its own dedicated app; new child safety and parental controls; and system improvements designed to make everyday tasks faster and easier.

iOS 27 supports the iPhone 11 and later, plus the iPhone SE (2nd generation) and later, although some Apple Intelligence and Siri features require newer hardware.

This guide covers iOS 27’s biggest new features, compatible iPhones and the latest beta developments. We also explain what’s expected in the next update, when it could arrive and which features are still to come.

What’s New in iOS 27 at a Glance

  • Siri AI: Apple’s new Siri AI combines personal context, onscreen awareness and web knowledge to deliver more natural conversations, richer answers, app actions and cross-device chat history.
  • Apple Intelligence across apps: Apple Intelligence expands across Safari, Photos, Messages, Mail, Calendar, Home and Shortcuts, adding smarter suggestions, automation, image generation and context-aware assistance.
  • Smarter Photos editing: Photos gains Spatial Reframing, Extend and an upgraded Clean Up tool, allowing users to improve composition, expand images and remove distractions more naturally.
  • Child safety and parental controls: New parental controls include Ask to Browse, Time Allowances, app schedules and enhanced Communication Safety tools. Activating the redesigned experience through Family Sharing requires every eligible family device to be running version 27 or later.
  • System Improvements: Apple has made many system operations faster and more efficient, which will be especially noticeable on older phones. Battery life may be longer, and there are dozens of small quality-of-life improvements throughout the system and its apps.
  • iPhone Handoff: iPhone Handoff in iOS 27 lets two eSIM-equipped iPhones share one number, switching calls, messages and Find My location when unlocked. It requires matching Apple Accounts and carrier support. T-Mobile offers it; Verizon and EE plan support. Fees may apply. More information below.

iOS 27 latest version: What’s in iOS 27.2

The first update was iOS 27.0.1, released on September 28. It fixed unexpected restarts following failed Face ID authentication, a 2x-camera color artifact affecting iPhone 18 Pro models, and an iOS 27 touchscreen freeze triggered by opening Notification Center and Control Center simultaneously.

iOS 27.0.1 also has a preventive role in a cellular problem that Apple did not mention in its published release notes. Apple has confirmed that a small number of iPhone 18 Pro Max models on AT&T can lose cellular service, preventing calls, texts and data access and potentially affecting 911 calls. Some owners reported their phones dropping into SOS mode despite previously showing a strong 5G signal.

The first major update for iOS 27 for all devices is iOS 27.2. It adds dual capture for FaceTime calls, suggestions in Messages, and adds several enahncements and new languages to Siri AI. On iPhone Duo it adds Edge Light and Apple Pencil support, too. Read more about iOS 27.2 here.

iOS 27 beta – What’s coming next?

  • Latest beta: none

The iOS 27.2 beta had included a redesigned Health app with AI-powered health insights, however this was removed from iOS 27.2 beta 4. The next beta, iOS 27.3, is expected to include the new Health app in addition to the new Siri AI audio features to Apple Watch series 12 and Ultra 4.

What features are still to come in iOS 27

At the time of the launch of iOS 27 not all of Apple’s promised features were available. Several were added in iOS 27.2, but there are still a couple that we’re waiting on.

  • Redesigned Health app: A completely redesigned Health app with AI-powered health insights is coming later in 2026.
  • Automatic password changes: The ability for the Passwords app to visit supported websites and automatically replace compromised passwords was removed shortly before release. 

What does Siri AI do in iOS 27

Apple

By far the biggest upgrade in iOS 27 is Siri AI – an entirely new architecture for Siri. Apple says it is more personal, conversational, and capable than the current assistant, with support for natural follow-up questions, personal context, onscreen awareness and up-to-date information from the web.

Siri AI features

  • More natural conversations: Siri AI can understand open-ended questions, follow-up requests and more complex natural language, making interactions feel less like issuing simple voice commands.
  • Personal context: Siri can draw on information stored in Messages, Mail, Photos and Notes to find details and answer questions. For example, you could ask it to find information buried in an old email or message.
  • Onscreen awareness: Siri can understand what you’re viewing and act on it, such as saving an address from a message, adding an event to Calendar or answering questions about an article.
  • Camera intelligence: A new Siri Camera mode lets you show Siri something through the iPhone’s camera, then ask questions or perform actions based on what it sees.

Alongside the headline AI features, Apple says iOS 27 includes a wide range of under-the-hood improvements designed to make iPhones faster, smoother and more efficient.

Apps can launch up to 30% faster, newly taken photos can appear in the Photos library up to 70% faster, and AirDrop transfers can be up to 80% quicker. External drive transfers should also improve, while updates to network performance and the system-wide search index are designed to make connectivity and finding information faster.

The company has also reworked core technologies including CPU scheduling, display performance and processing efficiency. These changes should benefit older iPhones in particular, with Apple promising smoother performance and more efficient battery use on devices as old as the iPhone 11 and second-generation iPhone SE.

Apple Intelligence interprets the request and assemble the appropriate actions across supported apps, potentially making Shortcuts significantly easier to use for people unfamiliar with building automations manually.

Calendar

Calendar can create or modify events from natural-language instructions.

Apple says the app can recognize contacts, locations, dates and other event details as users type, reducing the amount of information that needs to be entered manually.

Siri can also create complete Calendar entries for information that is on your screen in that moment, or by taking a picture with the Siri mode in the Camera app.

Image Playground

Image Playground is considerably more powerful and realistic.

Apple says it can create photorealistic images and lets users modify generated pictures simply by describing the changes they want. Individual objects can also be selected, resized, or repositioned.

AI-generated images will include a SynthID watermark identifying them as synthetic content. This particular feature wasn’t available at launch, but Apple has confirmed it is coming later.

Wallet

Wallet can create custom passes from QR codes.

Users can add their own fields and information to the pass, and passes automatically sync to Apple Watch.

Weather

Weather gets a clearer, more detailed forecast interface, with rearranged information tiles and new 10-day views showing precipitation probability/amount and wind speed throughout each day.

Home app

Apple Intelligence comes to the Home app for compatible HomeKit Secure Video cameras. It can group related camera notifications, describe recorded video and highlight clips that appear particularly noteworthy.

Maps

Apple Maps improves Flyover using higher-quality aerial imagery and Visual Intelligence models.

Apple says this produces sharper architectural detail and more realistic rendering of elements such as individual trees.

Podcasts

Video podcasts become easier to use, with improved controls for switching between watching a podcast and simply listening to it.

Fitness

Workout summaries have been redesigned to make them easier to share.

Users can also hide completed Fitness+ workouts.

iOS 27 changes beyond the iPhone

CarPlay

CarPlay gains an audio scrubber, giving drivers and passengers more direct control when moving through audio tracks and other content.

AirPods

iOS 27 introduces several new AirPods features.

A new Custom EQ lets users independently adjust bass, mids and treble using a simple three-band equalizer under Settings > AirPods > Audio and Routing > Equalizer > Custom.

Compatible AirPods also gain improved Precision Finding through Find My, making individual earbuds easier to locate.

Some features require both iOS 27 and compatible AirPods firmware.

Read How to tune your AirPods with a custom EQ in iOS 27.

Other changes in iOS 27

It’s not only individual apps that are seeing changes.

Home Screen and landscape mode

Apple is making iOS significantly more flexible when dealing with different screen orientations and sizes.

More Apple apps now work properly in landscape, including Health, Home, Music, Weather, and Watch. Dynamic Island and Live Activities can also adapt to landscape orientation. The Home Screen supports extra-large widgets.

These changes could simply improve iPhone usability, but they’re also well suited to Apple’s folding iPhone Duo.

iPhone Mirroring in macOS 27 has similarly become freely resizable, with Apple apps dynamically rearranging their interfaces as the window changes shape.

Liquid Glass refinements

Apple

Apple says Liquid Glass has been refined for better readability, more uniform refraction and improved contrast. A new slider lets users adjust the look from ultraclear to fully tinted, while updated icons, toolbars, sidebars and window shapes add polish.

Ringtones, alarms and alert volume

iOS 27 finally separates several sound-volume controls.

Instead of one combined Ringtone and Alerts slider, users can independently adjust:

  • Ringtones
  • Alarms and timers
  • Alerts and system sounds

The change is optional. Under Settings > Sounds & Haptics, turning off Match Ringtone Volume reveals separate controls.

Media and call volume continue to work independently as before.

Keyboard

iOS 27 introduces a new quick-paste control above the keyboard.

It lets you paste recently copied text, images or screenshots without having to long-press inside a text field, making everyday copy-and-paste considerably faster.

Apple has also made the Liquid Glass keyboard design more consistent across apps.

Privacy and Find My

iOS 27 introduces the ability to temporarily pause Find My location sharing without notifying the person with whom the location is normally shared.

Recovery and troubleshooting

Apple is also expanding the iPhone’s recovery interface, giving users more options for diagnosing problems and recovering an iPhone without immediately connecting it to another device.

System changes and how iOS 27 makes your iPhone faster

Alongside the headline AI features, Apple says iOS 27 includes a wide range of under-the-hood improvements designed to make iPhones faster, smoother and more efficient.

Apps can launch up to 30% faster, newly taken photos can appear in the Photos library up to 70% faster, and AirDrop transfers can be up to 80% quicker. External drive transfers should also improve, while updates to network performance and the system-wide search index are designed to make connectivity and finding information faster.

The company has also reworked core technologies including CPU scheduling, display performance and processing efficiency. These changes should benefit older iPhones in particular, with Apple promising smoother performance and more efficient battery use on devices as old as the iPhone 11 and second-generation iPhone SE.

Our testing of the iOS 27 beta supports those claims. On an iPhone 11 Pro Max, Camera launch time fell from 0.98 seconds in iOS 26 to 0.65 seconds in iOS 27, while Maps improved from 3.01 seconds to 1.36 seconds.

Everyday use also feels smoother, with more fluid animations, unlocking, Control Center and app transitions. The phone ran cooler during testing too, which could point to improved system efficiency and potentially better battery performance.

More broadly, iOS 27 appears focused on refinement rather than simply adding new features. Apple says it has addressed dozens of common user frustrations, while changes such as more adjustable Liquid Glass effects are intended to improve readability and general usability.

That focus should make iOS 27 particularly worthwhile for owners of older iPhones, even on models that do not support Siri AI. Those devices still gain performance improvements alongside features such as clipboard tools for the keyboard, independent alarm and timer volume controls, custom Wallet passes, Photos changes, larger widgets, and Liquid Glass refinements.

Child safety and parental controls

Apple

There are lots of improvements to parental controls, including new time allowances for entertainment, games, and social media, and new schedule tools for different times of day or days of the week.

This includes new features like an expansion of the existing “ask to buy” feature for apps to websites. Before a child can view a new website, they’ll have to ask for permission.

Ask to Browse: Ask to Browse will expand the current Ask to Buy feature to the web. Children will need to request permission before visiting new websites, and parents can review requests in Messages before approving.

Communication Safety: Communication Safety continues to help protect children from viewing or sharing nudity in Messages, FaceTime and other apps. Apple says it will also intervene before children see gore or violent content in shared images and videos.

Time Allowances and schedules: Parents can set Time Allowances across categories such as Entertainment, Games and Social Media. Recommendations are based on a child’s age combined with guidance from clinical and child development experts. Schedules let parents choose which apps are available at different times or on different days.

Redesigned Screen Time: Screen Time gets a redesigned interface with an at-a-glance view of average device usage and most-used apps. Apple says parents can quickly limit or extend access in the moment.

Child accounts and family safety: Apple says child accounts remain central to age-appropriate protections. Parents can manage app access, web access, communication permissions and Screen Time settings.

Problems with Parental Control set up

Updating the parent’s iPhone is not enough to activate the redesigned Screen Time experience. Apple says every eligible iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch and Vision Pro in the Family Sharing group must be running the appropriate version 27 software.

Devices that cannot run version 27 are listed as Legacy Devices and can continue using the older Screen Time and Family Sharing system. Apple says these incompatible devices should not prevent supported devices from adopting the new controls.

To find out which devices need to be updated go to Settings > Family > View Family Devices. Once eligible devices are running iOS 27, go to Settings > Family > Get Started to transfer the family’s existing parental controls or set up new ones.

Some families have encountered delays, outdated device listings and eligible hardware incorrectly appearing not to have been updated. Apple has acknowledged the rollout problems and says it is working to resolve them. If an eligible device is no longer owned or accessible, Apple recommends removing it from the Apple Account device list.

Accessibility changes in iOS 27

Accessibility features are smarter and more intuitive in iOS 27:

  • VoiceOver gives richer image descriptions and better understanding of onscreen content.
  • Live Recognition lets users press the Action button to ask questions about their surroundings and receive detailed responses.
  • Voice Control is more intuitive, allowing users to describe onscreen buttons and controls rather than remembering exact coordinate labels or numbers.
  • Accessibility Reader is able to handle more complex source material and provide summaries and translation.

iOS 27 compatibility

Roman Loyola/IDG

According to Apple, iOS 27 supports iPhones back to the iPhone 11 and second-generation iPhone SE, although some Apple Intelligence and Siri AI features require newer hardware.

Support for iOS 27 does not mean every device gets every feature. Apple Intelligence and Siri AI require an iPhone 15 Pro or iPhone 16 or later, while the most advanced on-device AI models require an iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone Air, or iPhone 18 Pro. On iPad, Apple Intelligence requires an M1-class model or the A17 Pro iPad mini, while the newest on-device models require an M4 iPad with at least 12GB of RAM.

There had been speculation that the iPhone 11 series and iPhone SE 2 would miss out on iOS 27 after leaker Instant Digital claimed on Weibo that the 2019 iPhone 11, 11 Pro and 11 Pro Max, along with the 2020 iPhone SE 2, would no longer be supported. That prediction proved incorrect, giving those models at least one more year of software support.

However, the iPhone 11 generation is nearing the end of its support life. As we explain in our guide to how long Apple supports iPhones, the iPhone 11 Pro and 11 Pro Max have already been added to Apple’s Vintage iPhone list.

  • iPhone 17, 17 Pro / 17 Pro Max (launched in 2025)
  • iPhone Air (launched in 2025)

  • iPhone 13 / 13 mini / 13 Pro / 13 Pro Max (launched in 2021)

  • iPhone SE 2 (launched in 2020)
  • iPhone 11 / 11 Pro / 11 Pro Max (launched in 2019)

The main dividing line for Apple Intelligence remains the iPhone 15 Pro generation: the standard iPhone 15 and all older models can run iOS 27, but they do not support Apple Intelligence.

Siri AI (All iPhone 16 models and later, iPhone 15

This release includes additional features, bug fixes, and security updates for your iPhone Duo.

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Tap General.
  3. Tap Software Update.
  4. Follow the on-screen instructions
